chunks: 1- Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from some of our companions, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā ibn ʿUbayd, from Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad al-Madanī, from ʿImrān al-Zaʿfarānī, who said:

I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Indeed, the sky remains overcast for us in Iraq for two or three days, so on which day should we fast? He said: Look at the day on which you fasted in the previous year, and fast on the fifth day.
2- From him, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Manṣūr ibn al-ʿAbbās, from Ibrāhīm al-Aḥwal, from ʿImrān al-Zaʿfarānī, who said:

I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Indeed, in winter we remain for a day or two without seeing the sun or a star, so on which day should we fast? He said: Look at the day on which you fasted in the previous year, count five days, and fast on the fifth day.

These two reports do not contradict what we have presented regarding acting on sighting, for the same reason that we mentioned in the first chapter: that they are solitary reports which do not establish knowledge or practice. Also, their transmitter is ʿImrān al-Zaʿfarānī, and he is unknown, and in the chains of the two hadiths are weak men whose exclusive narrations we do not act upon. Even if all of that were sound, it would still not oppose the position of sighting; rather, it would support it, because if what were to be observed were the number, then it would be necessary to refer back to it and not to the previous year and to counting five days from it. For the discussion concerning the previous year and by what thing the month is known in it is like the discussion concerning the present year, so that must necessarily be based on sighting for the report to have any benefit. The benefit in the two reports is that a person should fast—if his situation is as described in the two reports—on the fifth day from the previous year as a precaution, and he should intend by it fasting from Shaʿbān if he has no decisive proof that it is from Ramaḍān. Then afterward he should observe; if it becomes clear to him that it was from Ramaḍān, it has sufficed him, and if not, then his fast was supererogatory and he deserves reward for it.

3- As for what Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from a number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Ḥamzah Abī Yaʿlā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Abī Khālid, raising it to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
When the crescent of Rajab is established, then count fifty-nine days and fast on the sixtieth day.

4- And what Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb also narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Bakr and Muḥammad ibn Abī al-Ṣahbān, from Ḥafṣ ibn ʿUmar ibn Sālim and Muḥammad ibn Ziyād ibn ʿĪsā, from Hārūn ibn Khārijah, who said:

Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: Count Shaʿbān as twenty-nine days; then if it is cloudy, begin the morning fasting, and if it is clear and you looked carefully for it and did not see anything, then begin the morning breaking the fast.

The correct way to understand these two reports is what we mentioned regarding the earlier reports: that he begins the sixtieth day fasting on the basis that it is from Shaʿbān. Then if it happens that this is from the month of Ramaḍān, it is a day for which he was granted success; and if it is from Shaʿbān, then he has performed a voluntary fast for a day. What indicates that is his statement, “and if it is clear and you looked carefully for it but did not see it, then begin the morning breaking the fast.” For if the matter were as the proponents of counting hold, then it would be the thirtieth day of the month of Ramaḍān, not of Shaʿbān, because according to them it is never completed in any circumstance, and the state would not differ in it between clear weather and cloud. Thus it is known that by that he intended urging one to fast it with the intention that it is from Shaʿbān as a precaution.

key_terms.إِسْنَادِ: the chain of narrators transmitting the hadith
key_terms.احْتِيَاطًا: acting cautiously in religious practice when certainty is lacking
key_terms.الرُّؤْيَةِ: crescent sighting as the operative basis for determining the month
key_terms.الْخَبَرَانِ: the two reports under discussion in the legal analysis
key_terms.رَمَضَانَ: the month of obligatory fasting whose start must be established
key_terms.شَعْبَانَ: the month intended in precautionary fasting before Ramaḍān is established
key_terms.مَجْهُولٌ: an unknown narrator whose status weakens reliance on the report
key_terms.نَافِلَةً: a supererogatory fast if the day is later found not to be from Ramaḍān

ai.seo_question: How should one determine the start of fasting when the crescent is obscured and the sky cannot be seen clearly?
ai.summary: This passage discusses the legal ruling for fasting when the crescent cannot be seen because of clouds or obscured skies. It presents reports about estimating the day by reference to the previous year, then explains that such fasting should be done as a precaution with the intention of Shaʿbān unless Ramaḍān is established with certainty, while affirming that the basis of practice remains ruʾyah (crescent sighting).
